questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The amazing location, the many academic opportunities, the nice campus and facilities, and the interesting culture.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy. It can be found online on cal central and bcourses that you get access to when you get accepted.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: When you arrive you have the option to participate in golden bear orientation which is the equivalent of "intro ugen". You are in a small group led by two older students who tell you about campus and Berkeley. They had arranged a lot of activities and games to get you to know people in your group. I would definitely recommend participating, I made a lot of friends and I got more familiar with campus and Berkeley.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There is apartments and dorms and they are both hard to get. I was lucky to get housing at a dorm but would not recommend only applying for on campus housing. I lived at Unit 1 in a tripple with 2 american roommates which became some of my best friends. I can definitely recommend living at the dorms even though there is not much privacy in a small room where you have to sleep in bunk beds with 2 other people.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: When you get on campus housing you automatically get the meal plan as there is not really any options to cook for yourself at the dorms. The dining hall food is alright, they always have a lot of options and you can eat as much as you want. There is 4 places where you can get food on campus and a few stores where you can buy stuff with your meal plan.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is really fun, you will make a lot of friends. On campus housing is not actually on campus although it is only one or two blocks away. People will probably be a bit younger than you as most people who live there are freshmen.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It is hard to get and it is expensive but I liked it a lot.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You choose your classes online via cal central.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: If there is specific prerequisites you need to enroll in a class try emailing the professor and they will probably send you the enrollment code.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If there is specific prerequisites you need to enroll in a class try emailing the professor and they will probably send you the enrollment code. Should be easy to get all the classes you want, at least in the EPS department, all the professors are super nice.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I would recommend only taking upper division courses >99. I took one under division and it was pretty introductory. The upper division courses go more in depth as it is intended for majors of that subject. Also the workload of the course depends on the number of units. I would recommend the 4 unit courses because they cover more material and go more into depth.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There is more work at Berkeley, there is weekly assignments, midterms, big projects, and written exams. You need to work all semester to get a good grade.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 2 semesters

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: EPS 88: A Python Introduction to Earth Science, EPS 101: Field Geology and Digital Mapping, EPS 150: Case Studies in Earth Systems, EPS 183: Carbon Cycle Dynamics, EPS 178: Applied Geophysics

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
questions.answer: EPS 115: Stratigraphy and Earth History, EPS 118: Advanced Field Course, EPS: 103: Introduction to Aquatic and Marine Geochemistry, EPS 125: Stable Isotope Geochemistry, EPS 131: Geochemistry.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
EPS 115: Stratigraphy and Earth History and EPS 101: Field Geology and Digital Mapping: You go an a lot of field trips around the beautiful Bay Area. In 101 there is a field trip every week to the Berkeley Hills. If you like field work you should take these classes. Nicholas Swanson-Hysell is also an amazing teacher. 

EPS 150: Case Studies in Earth Systems: I learned how to think critically about scientific work and how to summarize and discuss articles I read. I also learned how to write abstracts in a concise and clear way. 

EPS 125: Stable Isotope Geochemistry, EPS 131: Geochemistry: Probably the classes where I learned the most. Berkeley are really good at geochemistry and the teachers are really smart and good at explaining difficult concepts. You will probably learn stuff you can not learn anywhere else.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Tennis, fitness, soccer, basketball, volleyball, badminton... There is also a lot of social clubs for almost everything and everyone.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Would recommend doing intramural sports, I really enjoyed that. Also go to GAB, the geologic association of berkeley or the ramsden room to meet other EPS majors.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
San Francisco, Oakland, the Berkeley Hills on the weekends. 
The National Parks in California are amazing would recommend: Yosemite, Death Valley, and Point lobos

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, people are super friendly. Try joining clubs or other activities and just talk to people in you classes. You will make a lot of friends.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Try joining clubs or other activities and just talk to people in you classes. You will make a lot of friends.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: That you have to be 21 to buy alcohol

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People actually really care about doing well in their classes. It is easier to find people who are really passionate about someting that you also like.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) apply for housing well in advance
2) join clubs and talk to people in your classes, and you will get many friends
3) go to SF and visit cool places around

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do not worry too much, also I would recommend 2 semesters.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
The academic experience was on another level, I have learned so much here. 
I have also never had so many good friends, I have not been bored since I have been here, there is always something to do.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
Took a little while to get used to only talking in english...
Also there has not been much time to do just nothing and not think about school.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
